Maya - run int8 vs float16 test and post results to shared drive (06/29)

summary: Weekly POC sync to review benchmark results vs AstraHealth's baseline provider. Redwood's hosted runtime shows lower p95 latency and higher sustained throughput for typical request mix; there are trade-offs on cost and tail latency on heavy-batched runs. Agreed next steps: share raw traces, run quantization variant tests, replay customer traffic, and prepare Dedicated capacity cost proposal.
transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining the weekly POC sync, I think we have about 45 minutes, quick roll call?
[00:08] Liam: Liam here.
[00:10] Priya: Priya on, Diego here too.
[00:13] Maya: Maya from Redwood, hi all.
[00:15] Noah: Noah here.
[00:18] Samir: Great, quick agenda - run through the benchmark numbers we sent, highlight deltas vs your baseline provider, discuss tuning levers, and agree next steps. Priya, any updates on the traffic sample?
[00:28] Priya: Yes, we should have an anonymized sample uploaded by Friday, just cleaning PII.
[00:33] Samir: Perfect. Okay Maya, could you walk us through the numbers?
[00:36] Maya: Yeah, so slide 1 - our p50 for the typical 512-token prompt was ~42ms on hosted with prefix cache enabled, p95 around 210ms. Baseline provider numbers you shared show p50 ~75ms, p95 ~340ms. Throughput for sustained 10k concurrent token/sec workload we saw 1.8k tok/s per GPU equivalent vs baseline ~1.2k. Cost per 1M tokens estimated about 18% lower on our config with batching and cache.
[01:10] Diego: Those p95 numbers look promising, the p50 delta is nice too. How consistent are those p95 numbers across runs?
[01:18] Maya: There's some variance. When we pushed larger burst traffic the tail did increase to ~280-320ms depending on sequencing and KV cache warmness. We attached raw traces in the sheet.
[01:28] Liam: Are those runs on the same model family we use in prod? Baseline is running model-x-v3, what did you benchmark?
[01:35] Maya: We used model-x-v3-base and also ran model-x-v3-quant (float16). We can run int8 as a follow-up - expected further cost reduction but need to validate quality.
[01:46] Samir: Important to call out the cache behaviour - with prefix/KV cache enabled the tail improves a lot for repeated contexts, which matches your conversational flows.
[01:55] Priya: How about throughput when you enable larger batches? We saw baseline throughput jump but latency spikes.
[02:02] Maya: Right, at batch size 32 p50 improved for batched workloads but p95 got worse if burst traffic and queueing occur. Our smart routing suggests adaptive batching - small batches for latency-critical routes and larger batching for background scoring.
[02:18] Diego: Can you quantify throughput change with batching?
[02:20] Maya: Sure, small batch (8) gave ~1.8k tok/s, batch32 peaked at ~2.6k tok/s but p95 jumped by ~120ms on the worst runs. Baseline provider also saw similar behaviour but overall lower max throughput.
[02:34] Liam: What about quantization experiments? You mentioned float16.
[02:38] Maya: float16 is our baseline for these tests; int8 quant can reduce memory and improve throughput slightly, in our past runs int8 cut latency by ~10-15% and cost by another ~12-15% but sometimes small hallucination/quality delta for certain prompts. We'll run those tests and include eval metrics.
[02:56] Priya: We need to see the quality delta on our eval set - small hallucination shift might be acceptable if within our SLOs but need the numbers.
[03:05] Samir: Agreed. We'll run int8 against your eval prompts and compute rouge/EM/qualitative pass rates.
[03:12] Noah: Also worth noting that on Dedicated pools the variance on tails tends to be lower since you avoid noisy neighbors; our estimate shows p95 could drop another ~30-50ms for Dedicated reserved capacity.
[03:25] Diego: That could be compelling. What's the pricing delta for Dedicated vs hosted?
[03:29] Samir: We'll include a draft Dedicated proposal in the next doc - rough estimates show higher fixed commit but lower unit cost for sustained workloads, we added a ballpark cost sheet in the drive link.
[03:40] Priya: Security checklist - SSO, KMS, audit logs - any blockers for us?
[03:44] Maya: We support SAML SSO, KMS integrations and can send SOC2 docs. Audit logs are available; for Private deployments we can do VPC peering or on-prem.
[03:54] Priya: Great, please send the compliance pack.
[03:58] Samir: Will do. Back to benchmarks - Lily (sic) the baseline runs you provided included some longer prompts, did you notice any model size mismatch?
[04:07] Priya: Some longer clinical notes as outliers, yes. We can tag them in the traffic sample.
[04:12] Maya: Good - those long-context flows stress KV cache and memory. We'll include a test focused on 2k+ token sequences. Expect higher latency but caching helps across turns.
[04:23] Diego: One of our concerns is tail latency under 99th percentile spikes during batch jobs. Any mitigation?
[04:29] Noah: Two levers - route latency-sensitive traffic to low-latency pools (smaller batch, warm cache) and route bulk scoring to high-throughput pools. Also model variant fallbacks if capacity constrained. We can demo smart routing rules next week.
[04:47] Liam: About fallbacks - do you have auto-fallback between hosted models to keep SLA?
[04:50] Maya: Yes, we can configure fallback chains by policy (latency, cost). If preferred model is overloaded, requests shift to a compatible variant.
[04:58] Priya: Any notes on instrumentation we should add to our client for better observability?
[05:03] Noah: Add request IDs, token counters, and KV cache hit metrics. We'll provide the SDK hooks.
[05:09] Samir: We attached a link to the benchmark spreadsheet and raw traces: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/astra-2026-06-24.xlsx - please review.
[05:18] Priya: Got it. Quick question - the cost numbers assumed rack-level GPUs?
[05:23] Maya: Yes for the Dedicated estimates we used A100-equivalent pricing; hosted blended rate is lower but variable. We'll call out assumptions in the sheet.
[05:34] Diego: Could you include a table that shows cost per 1M tokens across three configs: hosted float16, hosted int8, dedicated reserved?
[05:41] Samir: Yep we'll add that.
[05:44] Liam: Timeline wise, after we get the int8 quality results and traffic replay, realistic next milestone is a 2-week replay run in a Dedicated trial?
[05:52] Samir: Sounds reasonable. We'll prepare a Dedicated trial plan and a replay playbook.
[05:58] Priya: One more - can you share the exact test harness command or script so our infra can reproduce?
[06:03] Maya: We'll push the harness script to the shared drive, includes flags for batch size, concurrency, seed prompts.
[06:09] Diego: Are there any outstanding blockers from Redwood side?
[06:12] Maya: No technical blockers; just need the traffic sample and confirmation on eval prompts.
[06:16] Samir: Ok let's summarize next steps - Samir will send updated benchmark sheet and dedicated cost estimate by tomorrow, Maya will run int8 tests and post results end of week, AstraHealth will upload traffic sample and eval prompts next week, and we'll schedule capacity planning call for the Dedicated trial.
[06:33] Priya: That works. Thanks everyone.
[06:36] Liam: Thanks.
[06:38] Samir: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email with the links and dates.
[06:42] (end)
